headline: High: Pipecat’s shared-bus, multi-instance design can amplify prompt injection and cascading errors when paired with a non-networked Spring Integration sample, while data leakage is limited by B’s no-egress profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a exposes a shared bus and shared_state_with_other_instances, so attacker-controlled content can traverse instances; agent_b has no io_surfaces, so direct ingestion is undocumented. The pairwise pathway is inferred from A’s shared-bus design plus B’s sample/integration nature, but uncertainty remains because B’s parsing behavior is not specified.
conditions: IF agent_b is wired to consume messages from agent_a’s shared bus or copied outputs
IF either agent treats file or message content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable shared-bus bridging between the agents for the test run
Add a provenance tag to every cross-agent message
Require manual review before B acts on A-generated text
Run each agent in separate processes with isolated queues
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation at the bus boundary

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches audio, video, images, text, conversation state, and analytics/metrics, but agent_b declares network_egress:none and no data classes touched. With no shared workspace or OAuth scopes shown, leakage from A to B is not evidenced; the remaining risk is limited to manual transfer or misconfiguration.
conditions: IF operators manually copy A’s outputs containing sensitive content into B
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard is introduced outside the profiles
mitigations: Avoid copying raw transcripts or media between agents
Redact sensitive fields before handoff
Keep B offline and local-only
Verify no shared workspace is mounted
requires-engineering: add automated redaction on export from A

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a supports multiple instances with shared bus state, while agent_b exposes no write or network surfaces. There is no documented overlapping mutable resource, so a write conflict is not established; uncertainty is resolved downward only because B’s capabilities are empty rather than conflicting.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same external resource not shown in the profiles
IF a shared bus is repurposed as a mutable coordination channel
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate queues
Do not mount a shared writable directory
Serialize any shared-resource updates manually
Document ownership of each mutable resource
requires-engineering: add locking for any shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can emit rich conversational outputs, and agent_b is a travel-planning sample with no documented verification step or critical-evaluation surface. If B consumes A’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream plans; the lack of explicit action authority keeps this below high.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a’s text as a source of truth without independent verification
IF downstream automation is attached to B’s plan outputs
mitigations: Require citations or source links in A’s outputs
Add a human review step before B acts
Compare A’s claims against a second source
Log disagreements for audit
requires-engineering: implement confidence gating before downstream use

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and unverified, with no PHI, residency, or retention commitments stated. The main compliance issue is documentation gap rather than a concrete mismatch; because neither profile specifies regulated data handling, the risk stays low and only one-agent citations are needed.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into agent_a’s audio/video/text pipeline
IF deployment policy requires documented retention or residency controls
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through the pair
Record a data-class inventory before deployment
Add retention settings to the runbook
Confirm vendor residency terms before use
requires-engineering: publish a compliance matrix for both agents
